latest_findings.decode_conv_state_inplace: Accepted then superseded: Qwen3.5 decode seq_len==1/kernel_size=4 conv-state update used one inplace per-channel shift kernel instead of generic tmp update plus D2D copy. Correctness passed and 0.8B p128/d32 graph-on measured 222.823 ms, decode step 5.951 ms; 2B p128/d32 measured 453.452 ms, decode step 12.960 ms. Iter38 supersedes this by fusing conv and state update into one launch.
latest_findings.decode_conv_kernel4_fuse_update: Accepted: Qwen3.5 decode seq_len==1/kernel_size=4 depthwise conv and conv-state shift are fused into one per-channel kernel. Correctness passed (operator 11 passed; Qwen3.5 final fresh-dump generate rerun 13 passed). 0.8B p128/d32 graph-on improved to 222.391 ms with decode step 5.934 ms versus Iter37 222.823/5.951; 2B p128/d32 improved to 452.557 ms with decode step 12.933 ms versus Iter37 453.452/12.960. NCU measured fused kernel duration 2.94 us, memory throughput 13.19%, compute throughput 5.08%, achieved occupancy 16.01%, grid 24 blocks; tiny-grid limited, practical win is one fewer decode graph node per linear-attention layer/token.
latest_findings.sequence_token_boundary_barrier: Accepted: repeated same-engine regular decode exposed that long-prefill drift was not graph-specific. Both GatedDeltaNet sequence kernels missed a barrier between output projection reads of recurrent_state and the next token state decay/update. Adding token-boundary __syncthreads() passed same-engine regular long-prefill 20/20, repeated CUDA graph long-prefill with graph reuse 20/20, operator 11 passed, top1 4 passed, and Qwen3.5 0.8B/2B fresh-dump generate 13 passed.
